title: Shared primitives
description: Every artifact schema consumes these. Nothing here is specific to one type. Adding a primitive is a decision (notes.md #82); re-inventing one inside a type schema is the failure this file exists to prevent. DIALECT: JSON Schema 2020-12, chosen rather than inherited — composition behaviour is load-bearing here and 'JSON Schema' is not precise enough once it is.

artifactId.description: Stable identity for one artifact. The prefix names the type, so a trace reference is self-describing without a registry lookup — which is what lets #75's unresolvable-reference check run at lint time from the reference alone. Four digits MINIMUM, not exactly four: a format intended never to change must not carry a 9,999-artifact ceiling.

traceRef.description: One trace edge. Deliberately just an ID: the RELATIONSHIP is supplied by the field name that holds it, not by a value inside it. Named as its own primitive so every trace field in every schema refers to one concept.

traceLinks.description: A trace field. Always an array, never a bare string — a field that is sometimes one and sometimes many is two shapes for every consumer. Each schema declares its own named trace fields and annotates them with x-traceTarget.

typePrefixes.description: NOT a validation keyword — the authoritative mapping from #38's sixteen types to their ID prefixes, kept here so the pattern above, the allocator and the lint agree. Adding a type (#40) edits this file, deliberately.

notApplicable.description: #45. An explicit n/a carrying a required reason, so the lint can count *unjustified* absences rather than empty ones. Use as one branch of a oneOf on any field that may legitimately not apply.

payloadRef.description: A pointer to a canonical payload file governed by an ALREADY-ESTABLISHED format. Used by artifact types that wrap a format rather than define one — #8's dual-representation rule says an API spec IS OpenAPI and a data model IS a definition file, so the artifact carries the envelope, the trace edges and a reference, never a second model of the same thing. Two models of one payload is two sources of truth before the renderer exists. Each type narrows `format` to the formats it can actually render; adding one is a decision, because a format nothing renders is a payload nobody sees.

format.description: Narrowed to an enum by each artifact type.

path.description: Relative to the content root (#70) — never absolute, never escaping it. One resolver, so a path here means the same thing to the app, the lint and the typed tools.

nonEmptyString.description: A string that is present. Whitespace-only is caught by the lint, not by the schema — JSON Schema cannot express it without a pattern that is worse than the rule.

reviewStatus.description: Where this artifact is in the review workflow. Moves under human or agent action and NEVER cascades: an approval is not a change to what the artifact says.

lifecycle.description: Whether this artifact still stands. Separate axis from reviewStatus, because an approved requirement and a retired one differ in kind rather than in progress. Moving off `active` MUST flag everything tracing here.

materialityValues.description: NOT a validation keyword — the authoritative values for the x-materiality annotation (#61), which every property in every artifact schema must carry. structural: identity, lifecycle and trace edges. semantic: the payload a reader acts on. advisory: priority, ordering, estimate, workflow state. cosmetic: rationale, notes, prose.

artifactEnvelope.description: The fields every artifact carries regardless of type. Pulled in by allOf. Type schemas do NOT re-list these — they use unevaluatedProperties:false, which sees properties evaluated by composed subschemas where additionalProperties:false does not.

type.description: The artifact type, spelled as in #38. Redundant with the ID prefix on purpose: the prefix is for humans and cheap checks, this is what consumers switch on.

schemaVersion.description: #50. The content schema version this artifact was written against. Bumped on a breaking change to content shape, never on a tool release.

title.description: Short human label. Not an identifier.

supersededBy.description: What replaced this artifact. Promoted from decision to the envelope 2026-08-18 when a second type needed it (#114). The SHAPE lives here; each type narrows x-traceTarget to what may replace it, the same pattern as id and type.
